transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Michael O'Rourke (CTO, Apex), Sara V. (Head of ML), Tom Ellis (Procurement), Lina Gomez (DevOps)
Recording link: https://redwood/fireflies/ff-20260220-APX-7892 (internal)

Auto-summary (auto): Customer in active renewal window, interested in capacity expansion to EU and APAC and exploring Redwood Dedicated reserved pool for predictable latency; requested pricing scenarios and a perf run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick agenda — renewal timeline, region add, capacity and then action items. You all good with that?
[00:18] Michael: Yeah that works. Thanks Jordan. We're mostly focused on the renewal but want to lock down EU and APAC timing.
[00:30] Sara: Quick context, our traffic has spiked in EMEA so latency's been creeping up, and the dev team is asking about regional endpoints instead of cross-region routing.
[00:45] Priya: Got it. For context, we can either add hosted regions (fast onboarding) or plan a Dedicated pool in EU that gives you pinned GPUs and lower tail latency. There are tradeoffs on cost and autoscale.
[01:05] Tom: From procurement, budget line items — if we're doing 12 vs 24 months what's the delta? Also need an estimate for the EU node cost and add-on for APAC later.
[01:20] Jordan: We'll send a pricing matrix. Off the top, 24 months usually gets you a larger discount and fixed cap. I'll put together options: 12m hosted + burst EU, 12m hosted + APAC, and Dedicated reserved for EU with burst fallback.
[01:38] Lina: A question on networking — if we go Dedicated in our VPC, how does peering work? Does Redwood manage peering or do we provide config?
[01:50] Priya: Typically you provide the peering config; we provide the private control plane option. There is an on-prem package if you need air-gapped. Also FWIW KV cache and prefix caching can reduce cross-region token costs, but that depends on prompt locality.
[02:12] Michael: Can you clarify data residency? We need logs in EU for a subset of workloads.
[02:20] Jordan: Yes, we can scope specific routes to EU-only. We'll include a note about audit logs and KMS options for EU key material.
[02:35] Sara: Perf—what's realistic tail latency for a Dedicated pool versus hosted? Our 95th needs to be under 300ms for short prompts.
[02:47] Priya: With Dedicated pinned GPUs we see consistent 95th around 120–220ms for typical 8–16 token responses depending on model size. Hosted can vary more; with autoscale it usually meets 95th under 300ms but has occasional spikes during global burst.
[03:12] Tom: Are there SLA differences? We need uptime and credits in the contract.
[03:20] Jordan: Dedicated includes SLA-backed targets; hosted has best-effort tiers but we can add premium SLAs as an add-on. I'll flag the specific SLO language for legal.
[03:35] Michael: How does fallback work if a Dedicated pool is saturated — will traffic route to hosted models automatically?
[03:42] Priya: Yes, we can configure smart routing with automated fallback to compatible model variants or other regions. You can set policy to prefer latency or cost.
[03:58] Sara: We also want to run a perf benchmark with our realistic traffic (mixture of short completions and some long form). What's required on our side?
[04:10] Priya: We need a traffic profile (rps, token lengths, seq len histogram). Lina, can your team export a week sample?
[04:18] Lina: Yep, I'll pull the 7-day profile and anonymize it.
[04:24] Jordan: Great. We'll do the perf run in a Dedicated replica and share results. That will feed pricing and capacity recommendation.
[04:35] Michael: Any compliance paperwork we should expect? SOC2 plus some ISO docs.
[04:40] Jordan: We'll share our current SOC2 Type II report and the security whitepaper. On KMS, we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations; we'll include that in the packet.
[04:55] Tom: Legal will want to see data residency clauses and limited liability redlines — can you send the standard addendum?
[05:02] Jordan: Yes, I'll attach the renewal draft and the EU/APAC addendum.
[05:10] Priya: One note on cost optimization — depending on your workload we may recommend quantized model variants and prefix caching to reduce token spend without changing latency SLOs.
[05:25] Sara: Interesting, can you quantify the delta?
[05:28] Priya: We can run an eval on a representative prompt set and show token-cost delta; I'll include a small sample in the benchmark deck.
[05:38] Michael: Timeline: we want to finalize the contract in March, ideally by mid-March. Is that feasible?
[05:45] Jordan: Yes, if we get the perf run and budget sign-off this week or next we can get legal redlines and close mid-March.
[05:55] Tom: Procurement will aim for that. We'll share budget window by Friday.
[06:00] Jordan: Action recap — Jordan to send pricing matrix and draft renewal; Priya to run perf plan; Lina to send traffic profile; Tom to confirm budget; all good?
[06:12] Michael: Yep. Thanks, everyone.
[06:15] Sara: Thanks.
[06:20] End of recording.

Notes: occasional transcription errors in product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" came through as "redwood dedicate") and some speaker attributions adjusted post-call.
